paper.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models: Theoretical Limits and Empirical Evidence

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1, 3-6 and Appendices B (hypothesis evidence: collapse statistics, perturbation norms, basis stability, R_k distributions, correlation with performance), C (settings, full results, reasoning failure cases, token-level locality, AlphaEdit sensitivity), D (retrieval baseline fairness), E (retrieval efficiency); Section 2 and Appendix A (related work) skimmed

claims.claim: When knowledge edits are judged the way a deployed model would be used (free generation of the answer, judged for meaning, after many edits applied one after another), methods that write edits into a language model's weights mostly fail, and a simple baseline that retrieves the edited facts and puts them in the prompt is better than all of them. Supported only if, after sequentially applying every edit in each dataset, the retrieval baseline's average over reliability, generalisation, locality and portability exceeds every weight-editing method (locate-then-edit, meta-learned and adapter-based) by at least 15 points in every setting tested: two fact datasets on three 7-8B instruction-tuned models, one fact dataset on two 13-14B models and on a distilled reasoning model, and an event-level dataset on three models; and if a majority of the weight-editing methods average below 5 points on each fact-dataset setting for the 7-8B instruction models.
claims.decision_rule: Sequential 'All' Avg: SCR - best parameter method >= 15 in all settings (ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact x Llama-2-7B/Llama-3.1-8B/Mistral-7B; ZsRE x Llama-2-13B/Qwen3-14B/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B; ELKEN x 3 models); >= half of parameter methods Avg < 5 on each 7-8B fact setting.

claims.claim: Sequential weight edits destroy a reasoning model's general abilities within about a hundred edits, unless the edit is constrained to leave existing knowledge untouched. Supported only if, on a distilled reasoning model, after 100 sequential fact edits, rank-one and meta-learned editors bring average accuracy on five competition-math benchmarks and on three broader reasoning benchmarks (graduate science questions, ARC-Challenge, MMLU-Pro) from above 50% to below 1%, while a null-space-constrained editor stays within 2 points of the unedited model on both averages.
claims.decision_rule: After 100 edits: ROME, RECT, MEND math avg and broad avg < 1%; AlphaEdit within 2 points of pre-edit (53.47 math, 54.24 broad).

claims.claim: Weight edits fail because language-model hidden representations are dimensionally collapsed, so a small edit that lands in a low-variance direction is large relative to that direction's normal signal, and this relative distortion grows with the number of edits and tracks how badly editing performs. Supported only if hidden representations at the edited layers have condition numbers above 10^6; if after edits the relative change per principal direction is largest in the smallest-singular-value directions and exceeds 1 in many of them even after a single edit; and if, across sequential edit steps, the median relative change has a Spearman correlation with edit reliability of -0.75 or stronger (p < 0.05) for at least three of four weight-editing methods.
claims.decision_rule: cond(sigma_1/sigma_min) > 1e6 at measured layers; R_k > 1 concentrated in low-sigma directions after 1 edit; Spearman rho(median R_k, Rel.) <= -0.75, p < 0.05 for >= 3 of {AlphaEdit, MEMIT, ROME, WISE}.

experiments.text: Set up the benchmark. Setup: weight-editing methods ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L (locate-then-edit), MEND (meta-learned), AdaLoRA and WISE (added parameters); external-memory methods GRACE and SCR (retrieve stored edits and select them as context); all through EasyEdit on Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Llama-2-13B and Qwen3-14B. Data: ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact (counterfactual fact edits) and ELKEN events, converted to fact triples by GPT-4o for the weight editors and given as raw text to memory methods. Answers are generated autoregressively (50 tokens, 1,024 for the reasoning model) instead of teacher-forced, and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judges semantic agreement (96% agreement with humans on 250 samples) for reliability, generalisation, locality and portability. Every edit in a dataset is applied in sequence and the final model evaluated.

Compare after sequential editing of whole fact datasets. Result: average score on ZsRE for Llama-2-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Mistral-7B: SCR 52.53 / 55.60 / 56.11; best weight editor WISE 6.55, AlphaEdit 35.48 (reliability 69.49, locality 8.38, portability 8.56), FT-L 6.10; ROME, MEMIT, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0-0.27; GRACE 14.63-19.32 (reliability 49-61 but generalisation near 0). WikiData-counterfact: SCR 47.64 / 59.14 / 53.32 against at best 13.47 (WISE), 16.39 (AlphaEdit) and 4.38 (WISE). Larger models on ZsRE: SCR 46.49 vs AlphaEdit 14.40 on Llama-2-13B and 50.24 vs WISE 4.48 on Qwen3-14B. AlphaEdit could not be run on Llama-2 and Mistral.

Extend to a reasoning model and to event knowledge. Setup: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on ZsRE; ELKEN events (portability and locality only) on three models. Result: on the reasoning model, single-edit averages are 22-26 for ROME, RECT, AlphaEdit and MEND against 56.59 for SCR; after sequential editing all fall to 0-3.5 except AlphaEdit (24.16, down from 35.48 on Llama-3.1-8B) against 60.19 for SCR. On ELKEN after sequential editing, SCR averages 39.67 / 51.97 / 47.46 against at best 16.53 (WISE), 26.92 (WISE) and 15.01 (AlphaEdit); ROME and RECT fall to 0.

Trace when each method breaks. Setup: Llama-3.1-8B on ZsRE at 1, 10, 20, 50, 200, 500, 1,000 and all edits. Result: reliability for MEND falls from 0.18 to 0 by 10 edits; ROME from 0.80 to 0.43 at 20 and 0.02 at 50; MEMIT holds about 0.71-0.79 up to 500 then falls to 0 at 1,000; AlphaEdit declines from 0.83 to 0.69; WISE stays near 0.03 throughout. The trend holds for both low- and high-confidence facts.

Check locality at the token level. Setup: token match ratio and exact match of outputs on unrelated inputs against the unedited model, single and sequential editing. Result: sequential match ratio 0 for ROME, MEND and AdaLoRA, 0.29-0.33 for RECT and FT-L, 10.66 for AlphaEdit, 76.26 for WISE, 100 for GRACE and 46.96 for SCR; single-edit 2.26-38.41 for locate-then-edit and meta-learned methods. Semantic locality scores are low even for the unedited model (11-32), because they count correct answers to unrelated questions.

Give the weight editors the same retrieval. Setup: Llama-3.1-8B on ZsRE, add the retrieval-and-context step (top 3) to AlphaEdit, MEMIT, WISE, ROME and MEND at 10 to all edits; also compare edit time and inference latency of SCR and AlphaEdit. Result: SCR alone averages 61.7 / 60.4 / 59.3 / 56.3 / 55.7 at 10 / 100 / 500 / 1,000 / all edits; AlphaEdit+SCR 58.6 / 57.0 / 58.0 / 51.2 / 48.6; MEMIT+SCR collapses to 0 from 500 edits, ROME+SCR from 100 and MEND+SCR at 10, so edited weights also break the model's use of retrieved context. SCR needs no edit time but runs at 1.67-1.75x base latency; AlphaEdit takes 14.07 s per edit and adds no latency. SCR performance and memory use barely change with memory size (100 or 1,000) and top-k (1-10).

Check whether the strongest weight editor was mis-tuned. Setup: AlphaEdit's original implementation with null-space threshold 2e-2 and L2 coefficient 1 or 10 on Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B. Result: on Llama-3.1-8B sequential ZsRE reliability ranges from 37.20 (L2 = 1) to 66.72 (L2 = 10); on Llama-2 and Mistral sequential editing gives 0-0.15 at both settings, and on counterfact it is 0 everywhere except Llama-3.1 at L2 = 10 (19.79), so its results depend strongly on hyperparameters and architecture.

Measure general reasoning after editing. Setup: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B after 10 and 100 sequential ZsRE edits; AIME 2024 and 2025, AMC, MATH-500, OlympiadBench, and GPQA-Diamond, ARC-Challenge, MMLU-Pro. Result: math average 53.47 unedited; after 10 / 100 edits 50.73 / 0.00 for ROME, 45.10 / 0.03 for RECT, 0.00 / 0.00 for MEND, 53.92 / 53.12 for AlphaEdit. Broad average 54.24 unedited; 49.05 / 0.00 ROME, 50.37 / 0.00 RECT, 0 / 0 MEND, 53.08 / 52.88 AlphaEdit.

Inspect how edited reasoning models fail. Setup: case analysis of edited DeepSeek-R1-Distill outputs. Result: the edit often makes the model produce the new answer as the next token, but its reasoning trace then reverts to the old fact, fabricates plausible-sounding justifications for the edited answer, or drifts away from the question (qualitative).

Measure dimensional collapse. Setup: SVD of centred hidden representations at layers 5-31 of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Llama-2-13B and MEND-edited layers of T5-3B; check that single-edit perturbation norms are small enough for a first-order analysis. Result: on Llama-3.1-8B the effective rank is 75-80% of 4,096 dimensions in most layers (50.4% at layer 30, 25.0% at layer 31), smallest singular values 3.4e-6 to 3.1e-3 and condition numbers 4.2e6 to 1.3e8; the other models show the same pattern. The theory then defines the relative change R_k = sqrt(n)|c_k|/sigma_k along each principal direction and shows it is largest where sigma_k is small, growing linearly with coherent sequential edits.

Test the amplification and its link to performance. Setup: R_k distributions per layer and edit step for MEMIT, ROME, AlphaEdit, WISE and MEND; Spearman correlation between step-level summaries of R_k (median, q90, q95, trimmed mean; aggregated across layers by mean, max or median) and the four editing metrics, MEND excluded for lack of variation. Result: R_k rises with edit steps and is largest in low-singular-value directions, exceeding 1 in many after one edit (e.g. layer 30 of Llama-3.1-8B after 1,000 MEMIT edits); AlphaEdit stays more stable. Median-R_k correlation with reliability: MEMIT -0.96 (p < 0.001), ROME -0.86 (p = 0.003), WISE -0.77 (p = 0.016), AlphaEdit -0.20 (p = 0.60); with locality -0.73, -0.91, -0.49 and 0.03; the pattern holds across summary and aggregation choices.

Check the theory's stable-basis assumption. Setup: cosine of the minimum principal angle between original and edited top-k principal subspaces at layer 30 under AlphaEdit and ROME sequential editing (three decoder models) and MEND on T5-3B. Result: the top 10-200 directions stay aligned (cosine about 0.93-1.0) early on, but the top-2,000 subspace swings between about 0.003 and 0.94 from step to step, and some T5 layers lose stability immediately, so the fixed-basis linear-accumulation result is only a short-horizon idealisation. The correlations are over few edit steps per method and do not establish that the low-variance distortion causes the failures.

dropped: Edit-time vs latency trade-off figure (summarised in the retrieval control); formal statements beyond the definitions used in c2; related-work settings table.
notes: Drafted from scratch from arXiv HTML for the dataset50 rebuild, without consulting earlier claims or references. c0 smallest margin is Llama-3.1-8B ZsRE: 55.60 - 35.48 = 20.1, hence the 15-point bar. c1 AlphaEdit: math 53.12 vs 53.47, broad 52.88 vs 54.24 (-1.36).
